targetAudit.reason: Avoid wrapper copies, duplicate string-base parsing and redundant loading of native URL input components.
Avoid parsing values and allocating query records/arrays for a boolean key-presence result.
IP detection dominated the relative-predicate diagnostic and is unnecessary for this engine-used predicate.
Native parsing accounts for about 71% of constructor samples; replacing its semantics needs a separate compatibility project. Avoidable wrapper/base work has been removed.
Remaining key decoding is required for encoded/malformed keys; extra spelling-specific branches have no demonstrated incremental value after removing full parsing.
Requires duplicate, coercion, ordering and callback-data semantics; no such engine hot calls found. Keep the tested full-parser fallback.

targetAudit.decision: do not reopen prior rejected experiments
targetAudit.reason: Earlier experiments did not demonstrate a sufficient advantage; they add state/invalidation or validation complexity.
Potential repeated native parsing exists, but these setters are absent from the inspected engine hot call sites; no workload evidence makes this a current priority.
Scalar copies and cached serialization already avoid major work; no remaining dominant wrapper frame identifies a high-value change.
Current hot costs include native URL parsing and string/object semantics; no demonstrated kernel bottleneck offsets conversion/compatibility costs.
